title: Uber and China’s Pony.ai plan to launch robotaxis in London
summary: Uber and China's Pony.ai plan to begin testing autonomous Gen-7 robotaxis in London within weeks, marking an expansion of self-driving taxi services into a major European market.
content: The two companies said on Thursday that they would begin testing Pony.ai's Gen-7 robotaxis in London in the coming weeks.

title: Xbox is launching a new film and TV division
summary: Xbox creates a new centralized division called XP to consolidate entertainment ventures beyond gaming, including film, television, consumer products, and creator partnerships.
content:
Jack Black in A Minecraft Movie. | Image: Warner Bros.	

Xbox is launching a new division, called "XP," that's dedicated to Xbox experiences that aren't video games, including films and TV adaptations, consumer products, live events, and partnerships with creators and brands. Different teams at Xbox already do this work, but it will all now fall under the centralized XP division.
XP formalizes four "investment areas," according to a blog post by Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball:
XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling.

title: Vesta raises $30M to bring swarms of agents to mortgage lenders
summary: AI-native mortgage software startup Vesta raised $30 million in Series funding to expand its agent-based platform that automates loan origination for lenders.
content: Vesta, an AI-native software startup that helps lenders originate mortgages, announced a $30 million round led by Conversion Capital.

title: Cupertino might be made for your mom, but it’s a good take on tech
summary: CBS launches drama series Cupertino that uses contemporary tech controversies as storytelling backdrop, translating tech industry backlash into broadcast television drama.
content:
Ella Stiller, Mike Colter, and Rachel Keller star in Cupertino. | CBS	

Cupertino brings the tech backlash to the CBS procedural - an initially awkward combination, but with rewarding results. The show starts off just slightly unsure, but quickly figures out what to do with these strange times, creating fictionalized dupes of the Zizians, Polymarket, Jeff Bezos' looksmaxxing obsession, OpenAI stealing Scarlett Johansson's voice, and the fight for AI guardrails, among other familiar tales, and using them to speak to the feeling of helplessness in the face of rapid change that extends well beyond the greater San Francisco area. It turns out the seemingly outdated tools of broadcast TV are a fantastic way to tackle …

title: A senator tried to ban gambling on prediction markets—now she's a Kalshi lobbyist
summary: Senator Blanche Lincoln, who authored legislation restricting sports betting, now works as a lobbyist for Kalshi prediction market platform—a shift highlighting changing regulatory perspectives.
content: Sen. Blanche Lincoln wrote law that let US ban sports-event contracts. She lobbies for the other side now.

title: India rejects Elon Musk’s claim of discrimination over Starlink launch
summary: India's government disputes Elon Musk's discrimination claims against Starlink, stating the company is simply awaiting routine security clearance for commercial operations.
content: Starlink is still awaiting security clearance before it can seek spectrum and begin commercial services in India.

title: Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes

content: Get ready for more AI in your Windows and more AI on the desktop.
